correctness.rationale: For k the largest number of initial distinct primes with sum ≤n, choose j=k−t with t∈{4,5} of parity n. Then R=n−S_j is sufficiently large odd with R∼t p_j. The Matomäki–Maynard–Shao residue-uniform almost-equal ternary-prime proof can assign admissible three different classes mod 7 for every R mod 7, guaranteeing three DISTINCT q_i=(R/3)+O(R^θ)>p_j for θ∈(11/20,1). Appending these q_i to the first j primes gives k−1 or k−2 exact summands, proving 0≤k−L≤2. If n≡k mod 2, a k-part representation cannot contain prime 2 and its minimum sum is S_{k+1}−2; parity and n<S_{k+1} show iff exactly that endpoint. The published bounded-sum primorial envelope P_k≤H≤P_{k+1} and the constructed exact product ≥P_j give H/M≤p_{k+1}^6≤(2n)^6. PNT and AM–GM then show K/k→1 and log M∼√(n log n). Fresh dynamic programming checked representative n=301..1500 parity cases; finite checks do not establish the sufficiently-large threshold.
residual_risks: Asymptotic sufficiently-large threshold not effective; inequalities not asserted globally sharp, and other parity branch not classified.
The bounded checks are supplementary and do not replace the general mathematical proof.

value.rationale: Distinct-prime additive partitions and prime-product maximization are classical extremal questions. Constant loss of at most two parts for ALL sufficiently large integers, a parity-branch exact criterion and a polynomial multiplicative exact-sum completion bound are substantive quantitative bridges between different natural extremal objectives; neither follows from routine PNT estimates alone, requiring a deep almost-equal primes construction.
residual_risks: Possible implicit general additive-completion theorem is not exhaustively excluded.
